newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia says Annan good for United Nations.
newsitem.headline: Australia says Annan good for United Nations.

text.p: Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer on Saturday welcomed the selection of Ghana's Kofi Annan as the next U.N. secretary-general, saying his appointment would be good for the 185-member world body.

Downer said Australia had maintained a close working relationship with Annan during his term as head of U.N. peacekeeping and was impressed with his commitment to making U.N. peacekeeping more efficient.
"We look forward to working together with him on reform of the United Nations," Downer said in a statement.

"His nomination is good for the United Nations, at a time when the world body needs an able and effective leader who is sensitive to the demands of member states and realistic about the role the United Nations can play," Downer said.
Former foreign affairs minister Gareth Evans also welcomed Annan's selection, calling him "a man of formidable talent".
Evans, who knew Annan personally for some years, said the new secretary-general would bring first-class diplomacy and effective administration to the United Nations.

"It wasn't possible for the United Nations to make a better choice and the decision offers new hope and confidence of a new era of effectiveness for the United Nations," Evans said in a statement. "He is a fantastically good choice for the job."
Annan was chosen by the U.N. Security Council on Friday to be the seventh secretary-general of the world body after Boutros Boutros-Ghali's reappointment was vetoed by the United States.
